::: {#rem-replace-by-value}
#### Why this course uses functional programming

In a program built from pure functions (@def-pure-function),
an expression can be replaced by its value anywhere it appears
without changing what the program does.
That is what makes evaluation by substitution (@exm-substitution) work,
and it is also how algebra works:
$h(3)$ can be replaced by 3 in any formula.
So a pure function can be checked with the same reasoning as a formula,
and this course proves facts about programs that way.

`next_id` in @exr-next-id is not pure,
so `next_id() + next_id()` cannot be simplified to `2 * next_id()`:
the first returns 3 (from $1 + 2$) on a fresh start, and the second returns 2.
Racket can change variables too, with `set!`,
but this course does not use it.

:::
